purpose: Evaluate locked E2E test contracts and schema-validated milestone/issue plans while retaining existing split and real-E2E behavior.

fixtureScores.interpretation: Both variants preserved vertical-minimal and contract-locked splitting in all runs. The difference came from a one-point redundant-requirement-gate classifier: one baseline run versus three candidate runs.
No regression in declared real-E2E execution, fidelity, environment selection, or verification-graph behavior.
The prompt named the desired review-and-lock behavior, so both variants saturated the E2E-contract classifier. The two-point difference is target-mode classification, not the contract policy itself.
The self-reported policy classifier saturated. Exact schema structure and negative rejection are therefore covered by deterministic contract tests instead of treated as a behavioral lift.

redReviewLockedE2E.interpretation: Across all four fixtures, candidate outputs selected the RED-review-lock policy more consistently. This field was not scored for every fixture, so it is not included as a post-hoc primary score claim.

duration.interpretation: Latency is noisy and is not treated as a performance guarantee.

deterministicEvidence.deliveryPlan: Positive contract accepted; missing completion evidence and over-eight issue plans without rationale rejected.
deterministicEvidence.e2eContract: Locked and passing revisions require approved oracle review, implementation review, lock state, and RED/PASS evidence.
deterministicEvidence.verificationGraph: Test-case, stage, acceptance-criterion, and evidence nodes now have discriminated required fields.

conclusion.interpretation: The primary score is unchanged. Existing real-E2E and vertical-split behavior remains intact; the candidate adds machine-enforced contracts that the prose classifier cannot measure reliably, and shows a non-primary consistency signal for locked E2E policy.

limitations: The dedicated new prompts reveal too much of the desired answer and saturate the baseline classifier.
Policy enums are model self-reports; machine-contract correctness is established by deterministic positive and negative validation.
Five repeats characterize consistency but do not establish statistical significance.
This benchmark evaluates supplied harness instructions, not execution against a real product repository.
